items.summary: On International Men's Day, Women in Solar+ Europe (WiSEu) published a reflection celebrating men across solar and energy transition industries who mentor, sponsor talent, challenge stereotypes, and help build an inclusive workplace. The piece frames gender equality as expanding opportunity rather than competition, drawing on contributions from Antonio Arruebo of SolarPower Europe ('Gender equality liberates everyone'), Emiliano Bellini of pv magazine (advocating tolerance for mistakes when addressing bias), Josef Kastner of Nexun (who challenged inappropriate behaviour toward a female manager and stated 'Everyone deserves the same rights and opportunities'), Frank Niendorf of JinkoSolar, Kim Keats of Ekon Strategy Consulting ('Our industry is ultimately about people...'), and Jesús Alijarde of Ibersyd/Cerfo. It links these ideas to Movember's focus on men's mental health and argues that inclusive cultures are shaped by what leaders tolerate and challenge. The article promotes Solar+ Leaders, WiSEu's gender-open leadership development ecosystem built around mentoring and shared learning, while noting the views expressed are those of the author rather than pv magazine.
items.title: Women in Solar+ Europe Celebrates Men on International Men's Day

items.summary: Vincent Geloso's book, subtitled 'A New History of American Growth and Inequality, 1865-1945,' argues that the Gilded Age and Progressive Era saw far greater improvement in living standards than commonly acknowledged. From 1870 to just before World War I (the source text reads [q5: 191]), America experienced what Geloso calls 'the fastest and most stunning rise in the quality of life' ever recorded up to that point, benefiting especially the poorest 90% of Americans ([q1]). The period from World War I to the end of World War II brought slower but still substantial gains for those at the bottom. During these four decades (1870-191), living standards improved faster among the poorest [q2] than among the top 10 percent and as fast as among the top 1 percent ([q3], [q4]), which Geloso characterizes as a 'lean and mean egalitarian growth machine.' He attributes this dynamism primarily to America's market economy, which enabled people to relocate for better opportunities in industry or geography; while some government actions helped, he contends that market forces accounted for the lion's share of progress. Finally, Geloso argues that the American welfare state developed only after World War I because growth had slowed.
items.title: The Great Enrichment: A New History of American Growth and Inequality (1865-1945)

items.summary: A US-French man was convicted by a federal jury in the US District Court for Los Angeles on arson charges tied to the January 1, 2025 brush fire that ignited in the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area and grew into the destructive Palisades Fire. Prosecutors relied on security camera footage and cellphone location data showing he was the only person near the initial blaze; they described him as a former Uber driver who held resentment toward society and especially wealthy people, though he declined to testify at either trial. The fire killed 12 people and destroyed roughly 6,800 homes and other structures with estimated property losses of $150 billion (€136.7 billion). He was arrested in October 2025 after a prior trial ended in a hung jury that led to a June mistrial; prosecutors retried him under modified charges, and he is scheduled for sentencing on March 17, facing up to 40 years in prison. The defense contended the initial fire could have been caused by fireworks, which prosecutors said had no evidence of being set off.
items.title: Man Convicted of Arson in Deadly Los Angeles Palisades Fire

items.summary: A US congressional commission has warned that China's growing military partnership with Pakistan is increasing the risk of a two-front security challenge for India, urging Washington to deepen operational defence cooperation with New Delhi. The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC) examined this concern in a chapter titled 'China's Other Front: India and the Future of US Strategy in the Indo-Pacific,' noting that Beijing views India as one of the few countries outside the US alliance system with the demographic, economic, military, and geographic strength to challenge China long-term. The report referenced the May 2025 [d1] India-Pakistan military conflict following an Islamabad-sponsored Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people [q1], arguing it showed how China could support Pakistan during a crisis without directly entering the conflict. It highlighted India's strategic position, including its 2,100-mile contested border with China and location along key Indian Ocean sea lanes carrying significant shares of China's energy supplies and trade. The commission flagged China's expanding naval presence in the Indian Ocean as testing India's traditional advantages, recommending that Congress direct defence officials to strengthen undersea and maritime domain awareness through sustained operational coordination rather than periodic exercises. However, it cautioned that stronger India-US ties would not necessarily mean New Delhi aligns with Washington on every foreign policy objective due to its commitment to 'strategic autonomy.' The report's observations come amid efforts by New Delhi and Beijing to stabilise bilateral relations; in September, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping met at the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, expressing commitment to a fair resolution of their border dispute from a strategic perspective. A limitation is that these assessments derive from a single US congressional commission's analysis rather than independently verified data.
items.title: US report warns China-Pakistan ties raise two-front conflict risk for India

items.summary: On Friday, Haiti's government announced an agreement with El Salvador to build three new prisons in collaboration with a local company. The deal follows the deployment of 2,500 Salvadoran troops to help fight armed gangs who control some 70 per cent of Port-au-Prince and large parts of central Haiti; two soldiers were killed and two injured in an explosion while handling explosives at a camp. Haitian Justice Minister Patrick Pélissier made the announcement after visiting El Salvador, where he praised CECOT, its maximum security prison. The agreement comes as El Salvador has been under a state of exception since 2022 that has seen more than 90,000 people imprisoned without family visits, and Haiti's prisons have struggled with overcrowding after gangs raided the country's two largest prisons in 2024, releasing thousands. Pélissier said the prime minister had issued instructions to submit the project to relevant authorities to expedite it. He did not disclose how much the projects would cost, whether El Salvador would help finance them, or any management role for El Salvador.
items.title: Haiti and El Salvador Reach Prison-Building Agreement Amid Troop Deployment

items.summary: Ukraine's President Volodymir Zelenskyy sharply rejected US President Donald Trump's characterization of Russian leader Vladimir Putin as a "friend," insisting that for Ukrainians, Putin remains an enemy and a killer who continues killing people day and night. The remarks came after Trump described his relationship with Putin as a long-standing friendship ahead of a trilateral meeting in China on Thursday with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping; Zelenskyy argued the friendly framing sends Moscow the wrong message by reducing pressure to end the war, though Trump maintains that personal ties could help conclude the conflict. Separately, Ukraine faces an intensifying winter as Russia launched its largest attack of the year: a massive overnight assault involving more than 400 drones and 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic missiles, hitting bridges in Kyiv and railway stations in western Ukraine. The strikes killed at least nine people and damaged critical infrastructure just days after Ukrainian forces badly damaged the Crimean Bridge. With temperatures falling across a country already battered by nearly five years of war, attacks on power generation facilities, electricity networks, and heating systems raise concerns that millions could be left vulnerable to freezing conditions as repair crews struggle amid continued bombardment.
items.title: Zelenskyy rebuts Trump's 'friend' label for Putin amid winter bombardment of Ukraine

items.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs on Friday dismissed a United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) panel as biased and politically motivated, calling its claims that India is 'targeting' Muslims during the special intensive revision of electoral rolls (SIR) unworthy of serious consideration. The rebuke came one day after USCIRF quoted its head Asif Mahmood alleging that the Indian government was removing Muslim citizens from voter rolls, labeling them as foreigners and deporting them illegally amid Home Minister Amit Shah's characterization of India's Muslims as 'infiltrators.' MEA noted the panel has a documented pattern of issuing biased assessments. The controversy centers on the SIR exercise: its first phase ran in Bihar during 2025 (d3), expanded to 12 states and Union Territories late in 2025 (d4) with a third phase covering 19 states underway, while Home Minister Shah claimed three crore voters removed were Bangladeshi infiltrators. The Opposition alleges that 13 crore (q1) voters have been intentionally deleted from the rolls where revisions occurred. In its 2026 annual report (d1), the panel recommended designating India a 'country of particular concern' for religious freedom violations, though such recommendations are non-binding. Separately, on November 14, Indian Ambassador to the US Sharjeel Imam's profile was shared by the commission; he has been imprisoned over six years since the 2020 Delhi riots conspiracy case (d2), whose trial is yet to begin. The Supreme Court upheld the legality of the revision in May but clarified that it does not authorize deciding citizenship, while BJP-ruled states have used SIR results to deny ration cards and passport renewals. Nationwide protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar began on October 2 over alleged irregularities.
items.title: MEA Rejects US Religious Freedom Panel's Allegations Against India Over Voter Roll Revision

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the newly completed Nitish Setu, a six-lane cable-stayed bridge over the River Ganga in Vaishali that connects Patna to Vaishali and is named after former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. The event was framed as marking one year of the NDA government's leadership in Bihar, though it also drew political controversy because Nitish Kumar did not attend, fueling speculation amid shifting state politics; instead CM Samrat Choudhary and Union Minister Chirag Paswan were present. Alongside the bridge inauguration, Modi launched several developmental projects including 100 electric buses, highway expansions, thermal power units, and housing completions.
items.title: Modi Inaugurates Nitish Setu Bridge in Bihar

items.summary: In the first day-night Test between India and New Zealand at the Basin Reserve, KL Rahul scored his landmark 13th Test hundred (136 off 290 balls), becoming only the fourth Indian batter after Sachin Tendulkar, Mohammed Azharuddin and Rahul Dravid to score a century in all of South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia. His patient innings set up skipper Shubman Gill's aggressive 98 off 146 balls before he was bowled by Jacob Duffy; the two added 100 runs for the second wicket (Rahul contributing 165 in that stand). Rishabh Pant then scored his 22nd Test half-century (55 off 62 balls), and Rahul, Gill and Pant combined to post a commanding total of 486/4 at the close of play on day three. India lead by 118 runs but would want to extend their advantage further before lunch on day four.
items.title: KL Rahul's 13th Test century paves way for India's commanding lead over New Zealand in Wellington

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the six-lane Nitish Setu bridge across the Ganga, linking Patna and Vaishali, as part of a roadshow marking one year of the NDA government. The event generated political controversy because former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar—after whom the bridge is named—did not attend despite an earlier meeting with Modi; his absence was compounded by speculation following the omission of his photograph from official advertisements and a later rally in Raja Pakar, leading opposition parties to question his declining influence. Meanwhile, Modi's roadshow featured Bihar Chief Minister Satyendra Narayan 'Samrat' Choudhary and Lok Janshakti Party leader Chirag Paswan, signaling a generational shift in state politics, and he launched infrastructure projects worth 34,000 crore rupees during the visit. The reported tensions are attributed to these circumstances rather than confirmed by independent verification of their underlying causes.
items.title: Political tension rises in Bihar after Nitish Setu inauguration by PM Modi

items.summary: Former Australian cricket coach Darren Lehmann denied knowing of a specific conversation in which David Warner raised using sandpaper on the ball, as detailed by Cameron Bancroft earlier that week. He said he could not remember being present at such a discussion and attributed the difficulty to the event occurring eight and a half years prior. Lehmann acknowledged that his version differed from Bancroft's account of him contacting Peter Handscomb via walkie-talkie to have Bancroft remove sandpaper, stating instead that he only became aware of it after seeing footage on TV. He apologised for the team's culture during the 2018 South Africa tour, admitting attempts to achieve reverse swing "went too far" and describing his experience as a dark period from which recovery took three to four years; Lehmann also expressed empathy toward Bancroft and other players and staff while criticising doorstopping reporters. He denied intentionally avoiding questions about ball tampering but conceded the environment prioritised winning at all costs, and said he had no evidence supporting claims made by bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon, though he stated he trusted them. Lehmann confirmed he would attend Cricket Australia's independent forum on the tour to share his account, as have Cummins, Usman Khawaja, Warner and Bancroft.
items.title: Lehmann denies knowledge of 2018 sandpaper plan despite Bancroft statement

items.summary: PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss urged the Tamil Nadu government to declare the Cauvery delta districts as drought-affected and provide compensation of [q1: ₹40,000] (also stated as [q2: ₹40,000]) per acre to farmers whose 'Samba and Thaladi' crops were withering due to acute water scarcity. He attributed the crisis to Mettur Dam not releasing water for over a month, compounded by a Northeast Monsoon deficit, noting that discharge fell from [q4: 10,920 cusecs] on October 15 to [q5: 1,003 cusecs] on October 25. With the Mettur Dam water level at [q6: 61.53 feet] and storage at [q7: 25.84 TMC], he claimed available water could sustain supply for only about a week. He reported that crops, typically grown on over [q3: 18 lakh] acres, were restricted to around seven lakh acres this year due to anticipated shortages, with most now at the [q8: 40]-to-50-day stage and unable to survive another 70 to 80 days. Farmers reportedly spent between [q9: ₹25,000] and [q10: ₹30,000] per acre on the 'Samba' season by borrowing at high interest rates, risking an irrecoverable debt trap if crops fail. Anbumani demanded that a government team assess damage, declare the districts drought-hit, disburse relief of [q11: ₹40,000] per acre, waive land tax and levies, and grant full waivers of pending crop loans. He noted salvage would require substantial rainfall plus water release from Mettur in December and January.
items.title: PMK chief Anbumani demands Cauvery Delta drought declaration and ₹40,000 per acre relief

items.summary: Chief Minister Pema Khandu said on Saturday that Arunachal Pradesh Police has seized 18,600 kg of drugs and psychotropic substances worth around ₹75 crore since 2019. He added the force arrested 2,619 people in 1,452 registered cases over the same period while intensifying its campaign against drug trafficking. Khandu attributed part of this progress to Operation Dawn, launched in November 2023, which targeted 534 addresses and resulted in the seizure of 9,557 kg of narcotics. The remarks were made at a President's Police Colour presentation ceremony held Saturday at the Banderdewa Police Training Centre, attended by Union Home Minister Amit Shah.
items.title: Arunachal CM Khandu: Police Seized 18,600 kg of Narcotics Worth ₹75 Crore Since 2019

items.summary: About [q1: 24,000 properties] were without power Thursday during a mass blackout on the Eyre Peninsula. An intense storm damaged three transmission towers that operator ElectraNet said crippled the radial line powering much of the peninsula, including Port Lincoln; the company is investigating whether structural defects caused it but says this is unlikely and maintains its designs meet Australian standards. The mothballed, privately owned Port Lincoln power station—which will shut down permanently in [d1: 2028]—is temporarily servicing the region for several days while temporary structures are expected within days to improve reliability; there is still no timeline for permanent replacement of the damaged towers. Port Lincoln mayor Diana Mislov called the severe weather an unexpected event but urged construction requirements be met and wanted the plant maintained long-term as backup, also asking residents switch off solar panels per SA Police instructions. Premier Peter Malinauskas warned predicted Sunday storms and heat could further strain the grid; the Bureau of Meteorology forecasts early thunderstorms with temperatures reaching around [q2: 30] on the Lower Eyre Peninsula. Restaurant owner Craig McCathie said a multi-day blackout like in [d2: 2016] would be problematic if town reserves run out, noting his venue keeps about 20 hours of fuel but loses its back-up plan when diesel pumps go down.
items.title: Eyre Peninsula residents rely on temporary fixes after mass blackout leaves ~24,000 properties without power

items.summary: As China discards over 400 million smartphones annually, emerging markets in Africa and South Asia are increasingly sourcing refurbished devices from the country. Counterpoint Research reports that the global secondary smartphone market grew 13 per cent year-on-year in the first half of 2026 to 150 million units, driven by chip shortages and rising prices making new phones harder to afford abroad. Chinese buyers like Pakistani businessman Akhtar Muhammad purchase broken devices to export for repair, while Nigerian trader Mama reportedly bought around 40 used phones in a single day at Shenzhen's electronics markets, noting they are more expensive in Africa due to the absence of large suppliers. ATRenew operates PaiJiTang Mall near Shenzhen as a formalized self-service marketplace displaying over 20,000 used phones and drawing up to 1,000 visitors daily, with international traders making up about a third; Algerian shopkeeper Abdul Rahim flies there three times monthly to exploit a price gap of $110 to $132 per device. ATRenew's processing hub in Dongguan receives roughly 30,000 second-hand gadgets daily and is inspected by over 300 technicians before outbound shipments at similar volumes; Apple devices account for 70 to 80 per cent of sales, with the remainder split among Chinese brands. Counterpoint notes that older models like the iPhone 11, 12, and 13 are losing ground domestically but retain strong brand power overseas where they find a second life.
items.title: China's used smartphone trade expands to South Asia and Africa

items.summary: On Nov 21, South Korean President Lee Jae-myung toured a data centre under construction in the southeastern city of Ulsan and urged the country to move quickly as it competes in the global artificial intelligence (AI) race. In a public video of the tour, he said 'The whole world is competing right now, and speed is vital.' Data centres are described as a major source of chip demand, and Lee hoped that this project's success would draw further investment from global AI companies; the facility was built by SK Group, South Korea's second-largest conglomerate. The Ulsan data centre is being developed jointly with Amazon Web Services (AWS), with an estimated cost of 7 trillion won (US$5.2 billion) until 2029 according to South Korea's science ministry, and operations are scheduled to begin in the second half of 2027. SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won said in September that the capacity under construction was an initial 103 megawatt by 2029, with plans to expand it by nearly 900 megawatts in the future; he also noted the group is planning further partnerships with global technology companies as the project progresses. Lee observed that AI investment had mainly been concentrated around Seoul and said the Ulsan project showed regional growth was possible. After being told about 900 people were working at the site, he remarked that advanced facilities are short of construction workers and that ministries need to consider how to train the workforce for building data centres and AI infrastructure.
items.title: South Korea's Lee stresses speed in AI race during Ulsan data centre visit

items.summary: Rockstar Games reported that Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79bn in retail sales during its first day, which the company described as a new record for any entertainment product across all media. The worldwide figure reflects Rockstar's estimates through the end of Thursday, when the game launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, debuting in New Zealand before rolling out market by market at midnight local time. Rockstar also said it had sold 32.5m units during prerelease, a record across platforms. The company framed these numbers as entertainment's biggest launch ever, though the figures are estimates rather than audited totals and reflect only first-day retail sales plus prerelease volume. For context, the figure is nearly five times the roughly $800m that Grand Theft Auto V attracted in its first 24 hours during its 2013 release, and it exceeds Avengers: Endgame's total box office run of about $2.9bn worldwide after a rerelease pushed it past Avatar as the highest-grossing film ever. The game received critical acclaim with a Metacritic score of 99, which Rockstar cited as making it the highest-rated game ever, though this is based on aggregated critic scores rather than independent verification.
items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI sets entertainment sales record on first day of release

visual.alt: Bar chart. generated 3,790,000,000 $; figure 800 $; film 2,900,000,000 $.

items.summary: Wicketkeeper Bhavika Ahire has been appointed captain of the India U-19 women's team in a five-match T20 series against England U-19, with the first match scheduled to begin November 26 in Vadodara. Seam-bowling all-rounder Anaadi Tagde is named vice-captain for the same series. The fixture serves as preparation ahead of the ICC U-19 Women's T20 World Cup set for January 2027.
items.title: Bhavika Ahire Named Captain of India U-19 Women for T20 Series vs England

items.summary: A cold wave intensified across the Nilgiris district, driving the minimum temperature in Udhagamandalam (Ooty) down to [q1: 4.4 °C] on Saturday and severely disrupting normal life. Frost concentrated during early morning hours over low-lying pockets—Kandhal, Glenmorgan, and Thalaikundha—blanketing the landscape in white. Workers at Ooty's government Botanical Garden responded by sprinkling water over lawns to melt ice layers and prevent frost damage. The temperature dip also stimulated brisk trade among roadside vendors selling woolen caps, gloves, and winter wear as residents and tourists sought protection from the chill. Despite harsh conditions, the frosted meadows attracted photographers from neighbouring Kerala and Karnataka seeking to capture the seasonal phenomenon. Ornithologists and birdwatchers additionally reported a visible increase in native Nilgiri birds and domestic migratory species gathering on the frosted grasslands for food. The report presents these observations as local accounts of an ongoing weather event, with no quantitative baseline or forecast provided beyond the single minimum-temperature reading.
items.title: Cold Wave Grips Nilgiris: Ooty Minimum Temperature Falls to 4.4°C

items.summary:
Danmei—stories of romance between two men written primarily by Chinese women—is a genre that has grown steadily over the past decade on China's digital platforms, fueling a thriving industry of screen adaptations including manhua, animated or live-action series, and audio dramas. The roots trace to Japanese Boys' Love manga from the 1970s, which spread to China in the 1990s following economic opening; local fans then began writing their own stories as internet access expanded. Spanish publisher Norma launched a dedicated danmei imprint in [d1: 2024], now releasing two new titles monthly and drawing on works by authors such as Mo Xiang Tong Xiu, whose output reportedly helped put the phenomenon on the global map. Readers are mostly women aged 18 to 40, though academic Qi Zhang disputes that readers are predominantly heterosexual, noting queer people make up a significant sector of the community. Censorship has shaped the genre: authorities have detained and fined authors—most publishing under pseudonyms—and Qi points to the government's [d2: 2014] anti-pornography campaign as a turning point when platform Jinjiang renamed its danmei section chun'ai ('pure love') and restricted sexual content. In [d3: 2024], more than [q1: 50 people] publishing on Haitang, an erotic-fiction platform hosted in Taiwan, were detained or fined; the most high-profile case was Yun Jian, sentenced to four and a half years for obscenity after earning about [q2: 1.85 million yuan] ([q3: $274,700]) from [q4: 37 novels]. In [d4: 2025], Reuters documented another wave of arrests under regulations prohibiting obscene material; some investigated had earned only a few thousand yuan. These pressures have led authors like Xu Ren to avoid unofficial channels and reconsider where they publish, with fears that exposure could jeopardize their professional futures.

visual limitations: The source data references are not directly comparable for charting—Norma's 2024 launch is an event rather than a measurement; the detentions count (50+) refers to people on Haitang in one year while Yun Jian's earnings and novel count describe her individually, making cross-chart comparison misleading. No single measure ties these figures together over time or across groups.
items.title: Chinese danmei novels reached global audiences despite censorship and author detentions.

items.summary: Mathieu Potte-Bonneville, a philosopher and professor at École Normale Supérieure de Lyon who directs the Department of Culture and Creation at Centre Pompidou, is regarded as one of the leading experts on Michel Foucault. He became interested in Foucault through his involvement in AIDS activism alongside Daniel Defert, Foucault's partner, after reading The Order of Discourse; he also co-authored an illustrated biography with cartoonist Morvandiau and wrote Foucault: The Restlessness of History. Speaking at the Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona ahead of a sold-out event on Foucault's contemporary relevance in 2026 — the centenary of his birth, following Foucault's death from AIDS-related complications in summer 1984 — Potte-Bonneville explained that Foucault remains highly cited because he never stopped publishing and because his work spans philosophy, history, literature and social sciences. He noted major influence on Judith Butler, Achille Mbembe and Gayatri Spivak, describing the era as a 'neo-Foucauldian moment' or 'Foucault 2.0.' Potte-Bonneville argued that Foucault's relevance lies not in prophecy but in analyzing how surveillance and power transform over time; he cited an AI tool called Foukenstein created in September, which simulates Foucault's voice while showing only a turtleneck sweater to illustrate the death of the author. He also pointed to high school students carrying a 'Discipline and Punish' banner at a recent Paris demonstration as evidence that Foucault's message has returned to current events. On resistance, Potte-Bonneville said Foucault was cautious about the term but interested in moments when power is checked while enabling something new; he cited the 2018 Yellow Vests movement as exemplifying this ambiguity and highlighting an invisible segment of French society living far from decision-making centers. He concluded that a key lesson is to abandon apocalyptic narratives, since Foucault's work largely omits the future — when asked about it, Foucault refused to answer, arguing instead for engaging in politics in the present.
items.title: Philosopher Mathieu Potte-Bonneville on Michel Foucault's enduring relevance

items.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) clarified on Saturday that permission has been granted for a Pakistani delegation to visit the Taj Mahal, while its proposed visit to the Nizamuddin Dargah in New Delhi remains without security clearance. The delegation, led by Pakistan's Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination Musadik Masood Malik, will also visit other cleared sites including Humayun's Tomb and Dilli Haat. This clarification comes as the delegation arrives in India to participate in the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum being hosted in New Delhi from November 20 to 22; Malik was received at the airport by Pakistan High Commission's Chargé d'Affaires Saad Warraich and his visit marks the first by a Pakistani minister to India in three years. The forum, inaugurated Friday evening by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, focuses on shared civilisational heritage and follows a proposal made by Modi at the SCO Summit in Tianjin, China, in 2025. The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation comprises 10 member states including India (a full member since 2017), Pakistan, China, and Russia.
items.title: MEA Clears Pakistan Delegation's Taj Mahal Visit; Withholds Clearance for Nizamuddin Dargah

items.summary: Police in Maharashtra detained eight minors following a video showing a group of boys thrashing a couple with sticks at a garden near Phoenix Mall in Kurla, Mumbai. The incident occurred on Friday, November 20, when the juveniles allegedly made lewd comments while the couple took photos; upon objection, police say the group—consisting of about eight to ten boys—physically assaulted them, beating them with sticks and chasing them down a flight of stairs. Acting on the couple's complaint, DCP Ganesh Shinde registered a case under Sections 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352, and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The accused are to be produced before the Juvenile Justice Board. BJP leader Kirit Somaiya identified the couple as Hindus and labeled the boys 'Muslim fanatics,' noting that notices had been served on the parents of five of them; Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Intekhab Farooqui also condemned the incident, while Bajrang Dal activists protested against the park's watchman. The report attributes Somaiya's religious characterization to him rather than presenting it as fact.
items.title: Eight boys detained after couple assaulted with sticks at Mumbai park

items.summary: Waaree Forever Energies Private Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Waaree Energies Limited, signed a Power Purchase Agreement with the Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited to develop a large-scale solar power and energy storage project in Solapur, Maharashtra. The PPA was executed on November 20, 2026, following an earlier intimation issued on August 28, 2026, and disclosed under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. The project combines 700 MW of solar power generation capacity with a 700 MW/2,800 MWh Energy Storage Solution designed to store energy generated during strong sunlight for use when solar output is low or unavailable, thereby supporting more reliable electricity supply and grid flexibility amid the intermittent nature of renewable sources. The agreement represents a significant addition to Maharashtra's planned renewable energy capacity but does not include disclosed details on development schedule, commissioning timeline, or tariff structure; it establishes only a formal contractual step toward developing the project.
items.title: Waaree Forever Signs PPA With SECI for 700 MW Solar and 2,800 MWh Storage Project in Maharashtra

items.summary: During the festive season, Hoymiles India's team visited Setu Foundation to share sweets and spend time with children supported by the organization. The visit coincided with a company message linking community engagement to its 'Open Energy for All' initiative, which it framed as being about people as much as power. Monika Shekhar, Deputy General Manager of Marketing at Hoymiles India, stated that the team would continue seeking ways to give back to surrounding communities and described happiness like energy as best when shared. Setu Foundation works with children and underserved communities across education, healthcare, and skill development programs aimed at improving access to opportunities; however, the text provides no specific details on program scale, funding amounts, or measurable outcomes from this visit.
items.title: Hoymiles India Visits Setu Foundation During Festive Season

items.summary: Telangana Youth Congress (IYC) workers led by state president Jakkidi Shivacharan Reddy threw flower pots and damaged property at Meta's Hyderabad office on Friday, protesting restrictions imposed on the social media handles of two IYC office-bearers: national president Uday Bhanu Chib and national in-charge Manish Sharma. The protesters alleged political interference by both Meta and the BJP-led central government over accounts belonging to opposition figures such as Rahul Gandhi or posts criticising Prime Minister Modi, demanding that Meta reveal how many Indian accounts were withheld on government orders in the last six months and how many remain blocked, explain its automated blocking of certain content, remove restrictions they called unlawful against opposition voices, journalists, and creators, and respect India's constitution rather than BJP political institutions. In a post on X, the Youth Congress issued a seven-day ultimatum for Meta to "grow a spine" and restore the restricted accounts and posts, threatening escalation in courts, streets, and offices if demands were unmet. A simultaneous protest was staged by Mumbai Youth Congress president Zeenat Shabrin outside Meta's BKC office at World One, where demonstrators burnt a poster of Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also criticised Meta over the restrictions on X. The BJP condemned the vandalism as proof that the Youth Congress is "a party of goons," with spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accusing IYC workers of flaunting their destruction online, while Andhra Pradesh's BRS leader KT Rama Rao likewise branded them "goons" and questioned Rahul Gandhi over his approach to bringing companies into India. The reported restrictions on Chib and Sharma are attributed by the protesters as politically motivated but were not independently verified in the source text.
items.title: Youth Congress workers vandalise Meta office in Hyderabad over restricted accounts

items.summary: According to two people familiar with the matter, CrowdStrike is in ongoing negotiations to acquire rival cybersecurity provider Zscaler as enterprise customers increasingly favor consolidated security vendors. The discussions are not guaranteed and could end without an agreement. On Friday's close, Zscaler had a market capitalization of about $32 billion; its shares jumped 17 per cent in after-hours trading while CrowdStrike shares fell 8 per cent on the news. A combination would create one of the world's largest pure-play cybersecurity providers as companies seek to reduce their number of security vendors. CrowdStrike, founded in 2011 by George Kurtz and based in Austin, Texas, uses its Falcon platform for endpoint protection but has expanded into cloud, identity, and threat intelligence; the deal would address a gap in network security and help it compete with providers such as Palo Alto Networks. Zscaler, founded in 2007 by Jay Chaudhry, specializes in zero-trust, cloud-based network security that lets users access applications without traditional corporate networks. Any transaction would likely require backing from Chaudhry, who remains the largest shareholder. Bloomberg News first reported on the merger discussion.
items.title: CrowdStrike in talks to acquire Zscaler amid cybersecurity sector consolidation

items.summary: A magnitude 6.7 earthquake struck approximately 22 kilometers (14 miles) west-northwest of Ondores in central Peru's Junin region on Friday, according to the US Geological Survey. The agency initially reported the quake at magnitude 6.9 before revising it down to 6.7. It occurred at 7:09 pm local time (0009 GMT Saturday) at a depth of about 142.1 km (88 miles). The US National Tsunami Warning Center confirmed no tsunami warning, advisory, watch, or threat followed the event, and there were no immediate reports of casualties or significant damage.
items.title: Magnitude 6.7 Earthquake Strikes Peru's Junin Region

items.summary: An Indigenous-led conservation effort led by Maribel Pacco of the Pillco Grande Quechua community is documenting Andean bears (Tremarctos ornatus) using camera traps across Pumataki, a private cloud forest reserve in southeastern Peru. The team has identified 10 individual bears through their unique facial markings, providing some of the first local records of the species on the reserve and helping inform a Quechua-language environmental education program for youth. Pacco received funding from SPDA's Conservamos por Naturaleza grant to launch this initiative. Andean bears are listed as vulnerable by IUCN; Peru is considered one of their strongholds, with an estimated 5,000 individuals believed to roam the country. Pumataki lies in a buffer zone near Manu National Park and holds spiritual significance for local Quechua people. The project has also captured images of other species such as clouded oncilla, dwarf brocket deer, puma, opossums, and coatis. Despite limited funding forcing some plans to scale back, community members continue monitoring in groups of five while forming a management committee.
items.title: Quechua community in Peru builds up Andean bear camera trap project on their own reserve

items.summary: Professor Dame Henrietta Moore argues that AI raises a hidden "cognitive tax" by increasing cognitive load for the lowest-paid workers, who already face unpredictable pay, insecure housing and mounting debt. She contends that while employers increasingly value human judgment—according to the World Economic Forum, 59 in every 100 workers will need training to adapt by [d1: 2030]—automation also makes work less predictable through shifting schedules and adds mental fatigue from overseeing AI tools, straining minds already occupied by financial worries. Supporting evidence includes a 2024 analysis of [q4: 112,000 people] in the Journal of Economic Psychology showing that low-paid workers paid early were [q5: 7%] more productive and made fewer mistakes, and South African research finding men who retired at [q6: 60] rather than [q7: 65] showed slower memory decline. Moore also cites UK figures suggesting people facing insecurity across several life areas carry an earnings penalty as large as the gender pay gap that roughly doubles after seven years, and notes a Sam Altman-funded study found mental health gains from $1,000 monthly payments faded after one year—underscoring her view that universal basic services are needed. She calls on Britain's G20 presidency to require governments to assess how fiscal policies affect the cognitive load of the poorest people they touch.
items.title: AI's 'cognitive tax' falls hardest on low-paid workers

items.summary: Following recent scandals involving two iconic British comedians, the UK government is considering introducing staggered age-of-consent laws that would set different ages for sexual activity with men and women. In a discussion featuring Annette Young interviewing Katherine Allen from the Institute of Social Justice in the UK, the program examines whether such staggered consent laws are effective at protecting young people. The episode also addresses related social issues: the social costs of femicide, how loved ones cope with losing someone to such violence, and what support is available to families affected by these tragedies. Additionally, it profiles women challenging the male-dominated traditions of Mexican mariachi music. No specific data or statistics are provided in the source text regarding consent law effectiveness or any other topic covered.
items.title: Does staggered consent actually protect young people?

items.summary: Building on a 2024 collaboration, DNV, an independent assurance provider, and PLN Enjiniring, a subsidiary of Indonesia's state-owned PT PLN (Persero), signed a new two-year Memorandum of Understanding to broaden their cooperation in supporting Indonesia's power system modernisation and energy transition. The companies plan to expand the scope of services across consultancy and engineering solutions 'to support the continued development, reliability, and long-term sustainability of Indonesia's power system,' combining PLN Enjiniring's local knowledge with DNV's international technical expertise. Their prior collaboration has delivered planning and advisory services across the sector as electricity demand grows and renewable energy develops, though this transition requires greater system flexibility to integrate variable renewables while maintaining reliable supply. Over the two-year framework, the partnership will jointly explore digital transformation and engineering initiatives through a Jakarta-based team working alongside PLN Enjiniring's engineers; DNV VP Lena Landsmann stated that 'Indonesia's energy transition depends not only on adding more renewable generation, but also on building the networks that can integrate it reliably.' The text presents these plans as intentions rather than completed work. No specific projects, funding figures, or measurable outcomes are reported.
items.title: DNV and PLN Engineering expand Indonesian power-sector partnership

items.summary: Reed argues that skepticism of the AI trade is building, even as Anthropic's initial public offering proceeded well. The debut rose 17% over its initial price with a valuation of about $1.3 trillion, making it the biggest debut in history; yet shares fell 11% by midday and the broader market declined alongside them. Reed suggests some tech-industry observers would welcome a slowdown because resources are being concentrated among a small number of companies building essentially identical products, leaving little room for other ideas. He attributes this to an earlier 'tokenmaxxing' craze that accelerated revenue growth at frontier labs and hyperscalers but funnels every unit of memory and accelerator toward just a handful of players, which he says slows both innovation and AI adoption; these claims are drawn from his own experience with tech companies as well as a report by Wasabi and the Centre for Economics and Business Research. He also flags Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia as bad news for pro-innovation advocates: Huang championed open-weight models and a healthy startup ecosystem, and such models—many originating in China—had helped seed wider AI adoption that could slow if Chinese firms cannot access enough Nvidia chips. A further drag on development is the growing number of cybersecurity concerns worldwide, since AI boosts productivity for threat actors and hostile nation states as well as legitimate users. Reed concludes that while growth may still favor large tech players, real-world impacts of AI are increasingly expected to take longer than initially anticipated.
items.title: Anthropic's record IPO gives way to a cooling AI market

visual.alt: Bar chart. initial price with a valuation 17 %; Anthropic shares 11 %.

items.summary: Levent Alpöge, a technical staff member at Anthropic, announced Friday that he believes Claude helped him find a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. The claim is attributed to Alpöge and remains unverified: Anthropic declined comment via email from AP, and the Clay Mathematics Institute kept the problem listed as unsolved hours later. Formulated in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers toward infinity; it was selected by the institute in [d1: 2000] as one of seven Millennium Prize Problems with a [$q2: $1 million] reward for solution. Alpöge said his discovery came late Sunday night and that he messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei about 'my ability to announce' because the company was on the verge of its initial public offering, which raised [q4: $81 billion] at a [$q5: $1.5 trillion] valuation — described as the most valuable in history. The proof is presented within [q1: 17 million lines] of Lean code, and Alpöge said more than [q3: 250,000 pages] came from his work with AI; traditionally such findings would be published as a formal paper that readers verify line by line. Martin Bridson, president of the institute, called it an announcement 'of historic significance' but warned the journey to real understanding will be long and difficult. This follows September's OpenAI claim involving Navier-Stokes equations for fluid flow; Rutgers professor Alex Kontorovich likened the sequence of AI-assisted breakthroughs to an out-of-body experience.
items.title: Anthropic worker claims AI-assisted proof of Riemann Hypothesis; Clay Institute keeps problem listed as unsolved

items.summary: Some Amazon customers received a red "ATTENTION" banner on its website and app warning that the New York City Council is considering Intro 518, also known as the Delivery Protection Act. The notice stated the bill could increase fees for New Yorkers by up to $5 per order (q1/q4), framing it as raising costs just when making New York more affordable was needed. According to ABC7, the proposed legislation would require Amazon to directly employ workers currently handled through third-party delivery contractors, ending its reliance on that system; Mayor Zohran Mamdani backed the measure in August, while Queens Councilmember Tiffany Cabán is its lead sponsor and called it "a bunch of BS." Per Daily Express, Amazon said the bill could force it to move operations outside New York City, resulting in the $5 cost increase (q7), potentially hurting local businesses. The company cited a study it helped fund estimating annual customer costs would rise by approximately $400 to $660 (q8/q9). An "Act Now" button let customers email city councilmembers directly; Amazon reported receiving about 20,000 messages in the first six hours of the campaign's launch (q10). These figures are presented as Amazon's claims and projections rather than confirmed outcomes. No chart is warranted because the item contains no comparable readings or time series suitable for visualization.
items.title: Amazon warns NYC shoppers of possible $5-per-order fee tied to delivery-bill legislation

items.summary: As Anthropic celebrated its Nasdaq debut, CEO Dario Amodei reaffirmed the company's stated priority of AI safety and public benefit, warning that an "obsession with safety" is built into the firm's DNA. The IPO raised a record $81.3 billion from the offering, with a further $26 billion coming through a separate private placement, surpassing SpaceX and placing Anthropic among publicly traded companies worth more than $1 trillion. Critics question whether public-company pressures to deliver shareholder returns could erode this mission; legal experts say commercial demands may tempt decisions that hurt the stock price—such as delaying risky models—and note that safety choices made against the bottom line invite investor pressure. The company's structure is designed to protect its goals: it operates as a public benefit corporation with an oversight body, the Long-Term Benefit Trust, which appoints four of seven directors while founders control the other three, though all seven co-founders plus a shareholder majority could dissolve that arrangement and override safety decisions. Financial stakes are substantial—each founder holds more than $20 billion in company value, and its 5,300 employees hold an estimated $232 billion in combined equity—with non-founder staff able to sell up to 10% of their holdings on the first trading day; experts say these rewards may raise egos and influence how safety is weighed. Amodei countered that the company would pace development as long as necessary for confidence in safety, refusing business or political pressure. Anthropic's track record includes restricting access to its Claude Mythos model after testing revealed powerful cybersecurity capabilities, then introducing a similar Fable 5 model three months later with safeguards; it also partnered with defense contractor Palantir in November 2024 but resisted Pentagon use for autonomous weapons and mass surveillance, leading the government to designate Anthropic a national security supply chain risk. Separately, a November 2026 METR assessment found AI capabilities improving at roughly twice the previous rate, driven largely by AI-assisted research with no clear bottlenecks—raising fears of losing control over advanced models. Experts also note that few federal safeguards exist to shape these decisions, as the sector remains largely unregulated under a deregulatory White House approach.
items.title: Anthropic's IPO raises record $81.3 billion amid questions over its safety-first mission

items.summary: Filmmaker Vishal Chaturvedi, who wrote and directed the devotional drama Hanuman Ansh about Neem Karoli Baba (Maharaj Ji), spoke at the opening ceremony of the 57th International Film Festival of India in Goa on Friday. He said his film had been running in theatres for nearly [q1: 105] to [q2: 110 days], and described participating in IFFI as a proud moment, noting it has now run about [q3: 105] to [q4: 110 days]. Made on a reported budget of around [q5: ₹2] crore, Hanuman Ansh reportedly collected [q6: ₹452.86] crore worldwide, per industry figures cited by NDTV. Chaturvedi said his interest in the saint's life began several years earlier; he started discussing stories with a friend around [d2: 2009], and had been a devotee of Maharaj Ji since that same year before researching the film over subsequent years. He emphasized that the team wanted the film to be factually accurate, focusing on events documented in books or credible online sources. The article also notes his plans for other projects but does not provide comparable figures alongside these box-office numbers.
items.title: Vishal Chaturvedi on Hanuman Ansh's Box-Office Run at IFFI 2026

items.summary: Levent Alpoge, a technical staff member at Anthropic, announced on his website that he believes he has discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis using Claude. The claim remains unverified and would require independent confirmation by other mathematicians before it could be considered established; if verified, it would represent a major milestone in mathematics and AI's role in scientific research. Alpoge stated that his collaboration with Claude had generated more than 250,000 pages of mathematical material, though he noted he has not yet mastered all the mathematics involved. The Riemann Hypothesis, formulated by Bernhard Riemann in the 19th century, concerns the distribution of prime numbers—numbers divisible only by themselves and one—and is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which offers $1 million for a solution to each. Martin Bridson, president of the institute, called the announcement historic while cautioning that reaching genuine understanding will be long and difficult.
items.title: Anthropic researcher claims AI-assisted proof of Riemann hypothesis

items.summary: On Saturday, coinciding with its 75th anniversary, Google announced a commitment of around Rs 46 crore ($5 million) to IIT-Kharagpur aimed at accelerating advanced AI research and developing skilled talent. The investment is framed as part of India's broader push—led by Centre initiatives—to build homegrown artificial intelligence models and computing infrastructure under the Rs 10,371-crore IndiaAI Mission. Google CEO Sundar Pichai described the funding as a significant contribution to his alma mater. The article also includes an unrelated biographical profile of journalist Manash Pratim Gohain, noting his two-decade career at The Times of India and roughly 2,500 articles across education policy, politics, and governance reporting; this portion is not connected to the funding announcement.
items.title: Google commits $5 million to IIT-Kharagpur for AI research and talent development

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India is scheduled to meet senior officials from NBFCs on Monday, November 23, with Governor Sanjay Malhotra and the deputy governors expected to attend. The agenda has not been fixed in advance; an official told Business Today that companies will use such meetings to share concerns and suggestions rather than face a preset list of topics. Potential discussion items include microfinance loan issues, rural credit pressure from weak monsoon rains affecting farming households—echoing earlier worries about Maharashtra's drought-affected areas—and risks around gold loans after recent price declines, plus rising cyber-security threats following data leaks at two major banks in the past few months. A key demand raised by some microfinance institutions is to change the current rule that only families with an annual household income of up to ₹3 lakh are eligible for such loans, proposing instead a state-wise threshold. Separately, firms have suggested relaxing the requirement that total monthly loan installments not exceed 50% of monthly income; Deputy Governor Shreesha Chandra Murmu said any change would be considered only after assessing the need and cautioned against excluding part of the principal in calculating this ratio, noting the rule aims to prevent over-borrowing. No new regulation or decision is expected from this routine consultation meeting.
items.title: Microfinance firms may seek to change RBI's ₹3 lakh income limit ahead of November 23 meeting

items.summary:
A mathematician at Anthropic, Levent Alpöge, posted a four-page note claiming he had found a proof of the Riemann hypothesis with help from Anthropic's Claude AI tool. The problem was formulated in an 1859 paper by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann and concerns the distribution of prime numbers as they extend toward infinity. In his post dated Friday, Alpöge described how Claude "far outpaced" him near the finish line, noting that he had contacted Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei about announcing the discovery a day after Anthropic's stock market debut.

Alpöge linked to computer code written in Lean, a proof assistant for mathematics, which he says verifies his claim. Brian Greene, a professor of physics and mathematics at Columbia University in New York, called the proof potentially "one of the greatest mathematical breakthroughs in the past two centuries" and added that if true it would be "utterly astounding," given the Riemann hypothesis has been a towering target for nearly two centuries with profound ramifications.

Abhishek Saha, a professor of mathematics at Queen Mary University of London, said he believed the proof had a "very good chance of being correct." However, these statements represent endorsements rather than verification; Alpöge's claim remains an assertion that has not been independently confirmed.
items.title: Anthropic worker claims AI-assisted solution to Riemann hypothesis

items.summary: On November 21, Google announced a USD 5 million (approximately Rs 46.34 crore) funding programme for the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur as the institute marks its 75th anniversary. The grant is intended to accelerate AI research, education, and campus infrastructure while cultivating India's next generation of scientific and technical talent. IIT Kharagpur Director Suman Chakraborty noted that support for applied AI research was envisioned by alumnus Sundar Pichai, who praised the institute's work in Indic languages, agriculture, and education and linked the collaboration to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of making AI benefits reach everyone. The funding is structured around three objectives: advanced AI research across four priority sectors (Indic languages, agriculture, materials science, and educational technology); expansion of AI training for students, faculty, and teachers; and capacity building through internal AI frameworks and tooling. Separately, Google has committed roughly USD 15 billion over five years from 2026 to 2030 to establish an AI hub in Visakhapatnam as part of its broader Indian expansion.
items.title: Google's $5 Million AI Grant to IIT Kharagpur on Its 75th Anniversary

items.summary: The US has tightened advanced AI-chip export rules for five countries—Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore, and Brazil—by requiring BIS export licenses to ship them. The move aims to block China from accessing American technology indirectly through these nations' data centers; Jefferies warns it could also affect the global semiconductor supply chain and AI-sector investment. According to a Jefferies estimate, roughly 2.40 lakh Nvidia AI chips may have reached China since restrictions began in 2024, while Institute for Progress figures suggest Singapore's Megaspeed is leasing about 86,000 GPUs to Alibaba and other Chinese customers—indirect access the new rules target. Separately, Nvidia shares fell 11.5% on November 20 after reports of a possible US SEC investigation into accounting matters; Jefferies notes Nvidia has made around $61 billion in equity investments across the AI ecosystem plus $164.5 billion in lease guarantees and cloud-capacity commitments. China is strengthening its semiconductor industry, with HiSilicon, Cambricon, and Loongson on design; SMIC and Hua Hong manufacturing; Naura and AMEC making chip-making machines—projecting a 2025 equipment market of about $49 billion and materials market of roughly $16 billion. In Southeast Asia, Malaysia has announced around 61 data-center projects since 2023 with potential power needs up to 8.35 gigawatts, while Thailand saw approved foreign investment rise 64% in the first nine months of 2026, about two-thirds digital infrastructure; these countries may find it harder to source chips for AI projects amid Chinese ties. Jefferies suggests this chip war could reshape costs and supply-chain direction over time.
items.title: US AI chip export restrictions on five countries and their ripple effects

items.summary: A container truck carrying cars caught fire on Saturday evening near President Hotel on Indore's bypass, gutting three brand-new vehicles. The incident occurred after the container reportedly came into contact with a high-tension power line while traveling from Haryana to Indore; local residents say the tall container stopped beneath the line before flames broke out and spread rapidly across the cars as well as the truck's cabin and body. Of the eight Tata Motors cars being transported, five had already been delivered when three remained inside at the time of the fire. The driver escaped unharmed, and Kanadiya police along with a fire brigade team arrived to bring the blaze under control after considerable effort; officials are still investigating how the container contacted the power line and what caused the initial ignition.
items.title: Indore Bypass Fire Destroys Three Cars in Container Truck

items.summary: OpenAI made the full-duplex voice model GPT-Live-1.1 available in its API under the ID gpt-live-1.1, positioning it as an upgrade to GPT-Live-1 (which reached the API on September 10, 2026) and noting that OpenAI claims improved accents, transcription accuracy, number handling, and task completion over the prior version—though no benchmark scores were published for either model. The release introduces standby mode, which pauses inference during silence while keeping the WebRTC connection open; it is configurable via session.wake_policy.type (set to speech), an idle_timeout_s ranging from 5 to 60 seconds, and an optional vad_threshold between 0 and 1 with a default of 0.5, after which the server emits session.paused until user speech triggers session.resumed while retaining history. On billing, standby charges $0.02 per minute for idle WebRTC time versus $0.05 active—a 60% reduction—while backend model and tool usage are billed separately from voice minutes. The model supports multilingual audio input/output with a default context window of 128,000 tokens, turn detection, native ASR transcripts, streaming, function calling, and delegation to backends such as GPT-6 Astra or Luna (with instructions up to 16,384 tokens), but excludes image/video support, structured outputs, fine-tuning, predicted outputs, open weights, quantized variants, and published tier numbers. The model is API-only via v1/live/sessions over WebRTC or WebSocket, runs on OpenAI's cloud only, and follows GPT-Live-1 in powering ChatGPT Plus and Pro voice since October 15.
items.title: OpenAI Ships GPT-Live-1.1 Voice Model With Cheaper Standby Billing and No Published Benchmarks

items.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella praised Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang for building a resilient company, while cautioning that tech founders deserve celebration rather than hero worship. Nadella acknowledged that founders create something 'almost magical' by starting from nothing and can be singular in influence, yet he insisted they remain human figures who eventually die—drawing on his own experience with Bill Gates. He argued that lasting institutional strength comes not just from a founder's initial spark but from whether an organization survives independently after the leader departs; ideally, founders are happiest when someone else takes over and their creation endures beyond them. Nadella expressed distrust of leaders who claim institutions collapsed simply because they left, asking what such people actually built. He credited Huang with achieving this balance at Nvidia by building a durable institution capable of outlasting its founder. However, he stopped short of commenting on any potential return for Jensen Huang, deferring to the Nvidia board and noting that his admiration does not extend to deciding Huang's next move—claims attributed entirely to Nadella as unverified statements from an untrusted source.
items.title: Nadella praises Huang but insists founders are not gods

items.summary: Critics have long accused Apple of lagging in artificial intelligence, having entered the space only with Apple Intelligence in 2024 after OpenAI and other tech giants had already established themselves. The initial capabilities were considered lackluster relative to competitors, but over roughly two years Apple expanded its offerings substantially by introducing advanced tools such as a Siri AI chatbot, Audio Intelligence, and an additional tool called the 'intelligent assistant.' This rapid expansion has created confusion for consumers regarding what each offering does, which devices support it, and which features require payment. The article presents this lineup as a navigational cheat sheet rather than verified technical specifications or independent analysis of Apple's AI capabilities. Because the source is explicitly flagged as untrusted promotional-style content, its characterizations—such as claims about being 'late' to AI or that early offerings were 'lackluster'—should be treated as editorial framing rather than objective fact. As a single explanatory overview with no comparative data points across time, devices, or features, the item supports no quantitative chart; any visual representation would require figures not present in the text.
items.title: Apple Intelligence: Decoding Apple's Expanding AI Lineup

items.summary: The European Union and Indonesia officially signed a trade deal on Saturday (Nov 21) at a ceremony in Brussels, paving the way for it to come into force early next year. EU Commission president Ursula von der Leyen called it 'one of the most ambitious deals the European Union has concluded in Asia,' noting that together the two sides represent a market of [q4: 730 million people]. The pact is projected by Brussels to increase EU exports to Southeast Asia's largest economy by almost [q3: 40 per cent] within 15 years, and to lift economic growth with the EU's GDP projected to be [q9: 16 billion euros] higher and Indonesia's [q10: 27 billion euros] higher by [d2: 2042] than they would be without the agreement. Negotiations were concluded last year, almost a decade after being launched, as part of an EU push to diversify trade amid challenges from the United States and China. The Indonesia-European Union Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) alongside the ancillary Investment Protection Agreement (IPA) will open investment in strategic sectors such as electric vehicles, electronics, and pharmaceuticals. It removes tariffs on more than [q5: 98 per cent] of European exports to the world's fourth most populous country—including food, agricultural, and industrial products—helping save over [q6: 600 million euros] (US$[q7: 658 million]) a year in customs duties according to the EU. Around [q8: 90 per cent] of Indonesian exports to the EU will be tariff-free, benefiting top shipments including palm oil, footwear, textiles, and fisheries, per Indonesia's Minister of Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto. Palm oil and deforestation had posed stumbling blocks during negotiations; the pact includes mechanisms for cooperation on regulatory and sustainability issues plus a dedicated protocol on palm oil to address those concerns. The European Parliament must greenlight the pact and Indonesian authorities complete ratification before it can provisionally come into effect.
items.title: EU and Indonesia Sign Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement in Brussels

items.summary: The European Union and Indonesia signed trade and investment agreements on Saturday, ending a decade of negotiations by lifting 98.5% of tariffs on EU goods. The European Commission said the deal would create new business opportunities for both sides and project that exports to Indonesia could increase by nearly 40% within 15 years, while saving EU exporters more than €600 million annually in customs duties; sectors such as machinery and motor vehicles are expected to benefit most, along with new investment openings into electric vehicles, electronics, and pharmaceuticals. Trade between the two regions was valued at €28.9 billion in 2025, composed of €10.2 billion in EU exports and €18.7 billion in EU imports. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called it a momentous day and one of the most ambitious deals the EU has concluded in Asia. The agreements still require approval from the European Parliament and Indonesia's own ratification procedures, after which they could apply from early next year.
items.title: EU and Indonesia Sign Free Trade Deal After Decade of Talks

items.summary: During PPFAS Mutual Fund's 13th Unitholders' Meet on November 21, 2026, CIO Rajeev Thakkar said the fund does not chase companies expected to become 10-, 20- or 100-baggers. Instead, investment decisions are guided by business quality, financial performance and valuation rather than sector excitement. He illustrated this with a comparison of Coal India versus an unnamed hot-theme company: Coal India reported revenue of Rs 1.71 lakh crore and profits over Rs 33,000 crore at a dividend yield of 6.6% and PE around 7, while the other company had Rs 78,000 crore in revenue and under Rs 500 crore in profits with no dividends and a PE over 700 (still above 70 after threefold profit growth). Thakkar also argued that zero earnings-growth companies can be attractive if they distribute all cash flows as dividends — e.g., a stock at five times earnings paying out fully would yield ~20%. He noted the team does not predict quarterly surprises, interest-rate changes, FPI flows or geopolitical outcomes. On AI, he acknowledged opportunities but cautioned that excessive capex could disrupt the sector over two to three years and that open-source models may reshape competition; the fund favors companies with multiple revenue streams rather than those dependent on a single model. PPFAS's Indian IT holdings (TCS, Infosys, HCL) make up less than 10% of the portfolio. On mid/small caps, he said the fund invests when valuations are attractive but stays selective; small-cap returns depend heavily on entry timing and the global premium is declining. Regarding fund size, his AI-tool analysis found limited impact for large- and flexi-cap funds (larger funds performed better), while size matters more in small caps — with expense ratios and AUM growth pace also relevant.
items.title: PPFAS's Rajeev Thakkar steers clear of hot themes in favor of fundamentals

items.summary: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey criticized Meta on Saturday, arguing that its algorithms favor the ruling BJP by promoting accounts he described as 'demons and monsters,' which he said explains negative outcomes. His remarks came after the Indian Youth Congress staged protests outside Meta's offices in India, alleging that the social media company suspended or restricted the accounts of opposition leaders at the behest of the BJP. Dubey countered these claims by asserting that Meta had designed its algorithms to favor the Congress and urged it to understand this dynamic across X and Facebook. The IYC issued a seven-day ultimatum demanding restoration of restricted accounts and posts, naming national president Uday Bhanu Chib and national in-charge Manish Sharma among those affected. Protests also occurred at Meta's Hyderabad office on Friday with about 20 Telangana Youth Congress workers taken into preventive custody for roughly three hours before release, alongside similar demonstrations reported in Mumbai and Gurugram. The IYC threatened nationwide protests if restrictions were not lifted within the deadline. All claims of algorithmic bias remain allegations from both sides without independent verification.
items.title: BJP MP Dubey and Indian Youth Congress clash over Meta account restrictions

items.summary: This CGTN opinion piece, authored by international affairs observer Gong Rong (whose views are not necessarily those of the outlet), uses a social media exchange as its central case. An Indonesian user stated that during World War II Japanese forces occupied Indonesia for three and a half years, causing about [q1: 4 million] deaths; when AI platform Grok responded 'largely accurate,' a Japanese user accused it of betraying Japan and demanded information favorable to Japan. The author frames this as evidence of right-wing historical distortion shaped by decades of revisionism. According to the article, the AI's assessment drew on [d2: 1947] United Nations statistics and International Military Tribunal for the Far East archives, describing Japanese occupation crimes from [d3: 1942] to [d4: 1945], including forced labor, grain seizure causing famine, concentration camps, massacres, and human subject toxin experiments. The piece then attributes ongoing revisionism to Yasukuni Shrine enshrinement of Class-A war criminals with annual political homage, textbook changes swapping 'aggression' for 'entry,' the Nanjing Massacre being relabeled the 'Nanjing Incident' with a disputed death toll, softening of militarist symbols such as [q2: Unit 731], and crowdsourced rumor campaigns that feed doctored materials to AI. It cites an NHK poll showing agreement with the judgment that Japan's past war was one of aggression against Asian neighbors fell from [q3: 52%] in [d5: 1994] to about a third today, while as many as [q4: 48%] chose 'I don't know.' The author contrasts this with former politicians Yasuo Fukuda and Yohei Kono's acknowledgment of Japan's role as perpetrator (including the 1993 Kono Statement on comfort women), which it says is fading. The piece concludes that unchecked revisionism risks reviving militarism, invoking a UNESCO stele inscription about building peace in people's minds.
items.title: CGTN Op-Ed: AI Verification Exposes Japan's Historical Revisionism Over WWII Occupation of Indonesia

items.summary:
Chinese President Xi Jinping presided over the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province on November 19, 2026. The article frames this as a resounding success and a new chapter for global cooperation, with Xi calling for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the 'Asia-Pacific miracle.' He likened APEC members to passengers riding the same ship who must unite and look out for one another while navigating Pacific challenges. The piece emphasizes that China's hosting highlighted its economic transformation from a 1979 fishing village into a major metropolis, presented as proof that dreams become reality through hard work, creativity, and cooperation.

The article notes APEC was originally designed to strengthen economic cooperation amid growing regional interdependence, with three broad priorities: trade and investment (reducing barriers), innovation and digitalization (technology and AI), and sustainable inclusive growth. It stresses that APEC operates through consensus and voluntary non-binding commitments rather than as a military alliance or treaty-based organization.

The most noteworthy element was the historic first-ever face-to-face summit between Xi, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and US President Donald Trump, who committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security as a joint responsibility of the three powers. Following their meeting they released the China-Russia-US Heads of State Declaration Toward Peace, covering UN reform, energy security, and nuclear risk reduction.

The author attributes China's success in hosting to a focus on positive values rooted in Confucian ideals that 'harmony is of the highest value,' while contrasting this with European traditions. The piece also cautions that challenges remain: ongoing use of force for political objectives, rising military budgets instead of infrastructure spending, and humanity's need to stay vigilant—concluding that peace depends on economic development rather than unrestricted force.

The text should be treated as opinionated commentary reflecting the author's views (Stephen Brawer) rather than neutral reporting; its characterizations such as 'resounding success' are subjective assessments. No quantitative data or figures were provided in the source.
items.title: Xi Calls for Asia-Pacific Unity at 2026 APEC; China-Russia-US Summit Marks First Face-to-Face Meeting of the Three Powers

items.summary: In a bench trial over conditions at Florida's air-conditioning-free Dade correctional institute, plaintiffs' expert Stefano Shiavon analyzed data from [q1: 31 sensors] installed during the summer of [d1: 2025], finding heat indexes above [q2: 88F] ([q3: 31C]) for [q4: 97%] of recorded time, with a peak equivalent to [q5: 119F] in the H dorm dayroom at 10pm. Prisoners Dwayne Wilson and Gary Wheeler testified about heat exhaustion and suffering, while expert Dr Susi Vassallo linked long-term heat exposure to deaths including that of inmate James Beam, though a medical examiner attributed his death to pneumonia; she noted this case had unusually extensive internal heat data compared with others she has handled. The lawsuit was filed in [d2: 2024], alleging the extreme heat contributed to four deaths and constitutes cruel and unusual punishment, amid broader concern that more than [q7: 40 states] lack statewide air-conditioning policies for prisons; a separate Texas ruling required AC installation by [d5: 2029]. Defendants argued over [q8: 100 ceiling] fans mitigate heat and that the Eighth Amendment predates air conditioning, though Vassallo testified fans can raise body temperature at extreme temperatures. The Dade institution holds up to [q9: 1,500 people], and testimony is expected to continue.
items.title: Florida prisoners testify in Dade prison heat lawsuit amid extreme summer temperatures

items.summary: Joshua Foster of Essex was handed a €3,000 (£2,500) fine for causing death through a reckless act after his two-year-old son Jaxon fell 10 metres (33ft) from a fourth-floor window at the King Evelthon Beach Hotel & Resort in Chlorakas on 12 July. Prosecutors refused to drop the case, and Foster pleaded guilty during court proceedings where he said he believed the window was closed while showing his son the waterpark view before losing control of him; the boy died shortly after suffering severe cranial injuries from hitting a veranda below. The charge carries a maximum penalty of four years in prison but drew criticism from legal representatives, human rights defenders, media pundits and diplomats as lacking compassion, with prosecutors noting that although alcohol was detected in Foster's blood it did not indicate impairment to the point of recklessness; Judge Froso Christodoulidou described the incident as 'tragic' and imposed the lightest possible sentence rather than jail. Foster posted €30,000 (£26,000) bail to return to the UK for his son's funeral in August but was forced under threat of extradition back to Cyprus by 14 September after a clemency appeal to the attorney general on humanitarian grounds was denied; since returning home he said the family has focused on their surviving daughter. The account is drawn from Foster's interview with the Daily Mail and court reports, which should be treated as reported claims rather than verified fact.
items.title: British father fined after toddler's fatal fall from Cyprus hotel window recalls 'despair'

items.summary: Diplomats at a United Nations meeting in Geneva agreed to begin discussing options to regulate lethal autonomous weapons, but the compromise fell far short of what humanitarian groups and many countries had hoped. After negotiations that ran until 4:30 a.m. Saturday, delegates settled on giving nations two years to propose regulations that could be legally binding or merely optional — explicitly rejecting an agreement within one year. The ICRC, which called for urgent rules before talks began, said it regretted the outcome and renewed its appeal for a binding treaty; other campaigners dismissed the deal as "a nothing burger" and warned people may die because of it.
